subject: Specifying Covariances with WLSMV and ordered data: can it be done?

messages.author: 75b75ee829b961b7
messages.subject: Specifying Covariances with WLSMV and ordered data: can it be done?
parts:
Dear Group,


I have generated a model while using the ordered argument and WLSMV as the estimator. Ideally I would like to specify a relationship between two variables as a covariance but while attempting to do so I receive an error message:

I have provided the code and message below.


SM2B <-"
## Measurement model ##
PS ~ PB + PF + cIT + cET + crS + crR + GEOR + cADT + cAWS + SS + D
##
cET ~ COS + SIN
crS ~ COS + SIN
crR ~ COS + SIN
##
COS ~~ SIN"

SEM2B <- sem(SM2B, ordered=c("PS"), data = FCSH)

##
Error in vnames(FLAT, type = "ov.x", ov.x.fatal = TRUE) : 
  lavaan ERROR: model syntax contains variance/covariance/intercept formulas
  involving (an) exogenous variable(s): [COS SIN];
  Please remove them and try again.

I apologize in advance if I am missing something fundamental and obvious. I am a relative newcomer to SEM in general. Is there there a work-around or secondary option that I can follow that will allow me to specify this relationship?  

Thank you for you time.

Andrew

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Specifying Covariances with WLSMV and ordered data: can it be done?
parts: Those variables are just exogenous predictors.  You don't need to treat them as random variables to find out their covariance, you can just use the cov() function.  All exogenous predictors are allowed to be correlated, even if that information isn't a model parameter (like in OLS regression), but if you want to include those estimates in your model, you can try this:

SM2B <-"
## Measurement model ##
PS ~ PB + PF + cIT + cET + crS + crR + GEOR + cADT + cAWS + SS + D
##
cET ~ COS + SIN
crS ~ COS + SIN
crR ~ COS + SIN
"

SEM2B <- sem(SM2B, ordered=c("PS"), data = FCSH, fixed.x = FALSE)


Terry

Best wishes

messages.author: 89c9fc822e34b78c
messages.subject: Re: Specifying Covariances with WLSMV and ordered data: can it be done?
parts:
On 03/09/2015 11:26 AM, andrew...@ncl.ac.uk wrote:
> Thank you for your reply. I tried this but unfortunately fixed.x
> argument does not work with WLSMV estimators.

You should understand that the 'x' variables are usually not part of the
model, if you are using WLSMV. Their variaces AND covariances are simply
fixed at their sample-based values.

If you really want to bring them into the model, you can 'upgrade' them
to latent variables, by specifying a factor with a single indicator with
a fixed-to-one loading, and a residual variance fixed to zero.

Yves.
